नन्द: Nanda m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 12, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7.

Nanda m.: Name of a drum (मृदङ्ग). One of the two drums (the other being Upananda), of suitable size, producing sweet sound at the crest of the flag of Yudhiṣṭhira (यस्य ध्वजाग्रे नदतो मृदङ्गौ नन्दो-पन्दौ मधुरौ युक्तरूपौ) 3. 254. 6.
नन्दक: Nandaka m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 11, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7.

Nandaka m.: Name of the sword of Kṛṣṇa (Viṣṇu). It appeared from Kṛṣṇa's body (together with his conch, disk, mace etc.) when he laughed to show his terrible form to Duryo-dhana and others in the Sabhā of the Kauravas 5. 129. 9; (hence Nandakin one of the thousand names of Viṣṇu 13. 135. 120).
नन्दिनी: Nandinī (Nandī) f.: A mythical cow. A. Birth: Born of Surabhī, Dakṣa's daughter, and Kaśyapa 1. 93. 8; also called Nandī 1. 165. 15, 24, 25. B. Qualities and Description: She was capable of fulfill-ing all desires, hence called सर्वकामदुघा 1. 93. 9, सर्वकामदुह् 1. 93. 13; 1. 165. 9-11; the best cow (उत्तमा गौः) 1. 93. 18, 13; the mortal who drank her milk lived for ten thousand years, remaining young all along (स्थिरयौवनः) 1. 93. 19; description 1. 93. 15, 31; 1. 165. 13, 14, 21. C. Asso-ciation with Vasiṣṭha: She was given to Vasiṣṭha (son of Varuṇa) as his होमधेनु (who supplied milk for giving oblations); she was seen moving in the forest by the wife of Dyaus, one of the eight Vasus 1. 93. 13; at her request Dyaus, together with other Vasus, abducted Nandinī and her calf to be given away to princess Jinavatī who was a friend of the wife of Dyaus 1. 93. 26, 28, 21-23; [when cursed by Vasiṣṭha (1. 93. 31) the Vasus possibly returned Nandinī and her calf to Vasiṣṭha 1. 93, 34]. D. Conflict between Vasiṣṭha and Viśvāmitra: Viśvā-mitra, while on a visit to Vasiṣṭha, was sur-prised at the qualities of Nandinī; he asked Vasiṣṭha to give her to him in exchange for an अर्बुद cows or even his kingdom; Vasiṣṭha declined to part with Nandinī as she was needed for the worship of gods, guests and manes; Viśvāmitra then declared his intention to forcibly take her away; Viśvāmitra and his army used force to take her away; they beat her with whips, rods and stones and bound her calf with a rope; lowing she appro-ached Vasiṣṭha; when she knew that Vasiṣṭha would not do anything to stop Viśvāmitra out of forbearance and also that his non-intervention did not mean he wanted to forsake her she assumed a terrible form (प्रबभौ घोरदर्शना) and produced from parts of her body and excretions various tribes like Pahlavas, Śakas, Śabaras and others equipped with weapons; Viśvāmitra's army was routed and his attempt to take away Nandinī was foiled 1. 165. 2-40.
Nandinī f.: Name of a holy well (कूप). Described as frequented by gods (त्रिदशसेवित); one who visits it gets the merit of a Naramedha 3. 82. 134.
नल: Nala m.: A monkey-chief. A. Birth: Son of God Tvaṣṭṛ, Viśva-karman 3 267. 41. B. Skill: As an excellent builder, he was respected by the artisans (शिल्पिसंमतः) 3. 267. 41; whatever wood, or straw, or stone he might throw in the ocean that would not sink; at the suggestion of the ocean, who appeared before Rāma, he was asked to build a bridge across the ocean; this bridge is even now known as Nalasetu which in appearance is like a mountain (गिरिसंनिभः) 3. 267. 43-45. C. Part in the war: He was one of the monkey-chiefs who protected Rāma's army of monkeys on its way to the southern ocean 3. 267. 19; he fought a duel with the demon Tuṇḍa 3. 269. 8; he, with other monkey-chiefs, watched over the bodies of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa lying on the ground tied by the arrows of Indrajit 3. 273. 4; Nala and other monkey-chiefs together with their armies surrounded Rāvaṇa as he was rushing against Rāma and destroyed Rāvaṇa's army with trees 3. 274. 3-4.
नहुष: Nahuṣa m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 9, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7; also listed by Sūta among the sons of Kadrū 1. 31. 9, 2.
नागाशिन्: Nāgāśin m.: A mythical bird, living in the world of Suparṇas 5. 99. 9, 1. Born in the कुल of Vainateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; feeding on serpents; marked with श्रीवत्स, his deity is Viṣṇu; by action a Kṣatriya, not obtaining Brahminhood because indulging in destroying his kinsmen 5. 99. 2-8.
नाडीजङ्घ: Nāḍījaṅgha m.: A mythical crane, also called Rājadharman 12. 163. 19. A. Birth: Son of a देवकन्या and Kaśyapa 12. 163. 18, 19. B. Residence: Lake Inradyumna 3. 191. 9. C. Description: Learned (महाप्रज्ञः, विद्वान् 12, 163. 18, 19), lustrous like the chief of gods, adorned with bright ornaments of gold, blazing with lustre 12. 163. 19, 20. D. Status: Best among the birds (खगोत्तम), king of the cranes (बकराज); unrivalled on the earth; as friend of god Brahman, he used to visit the world of Brahman 12. 163. 17-19. E. Age: Of fabulous age, older then the owl Prākāra-karṇa; Nāḍījaṅgha directed the royal sage Indradyumna to the tortoise Akūpāra who was older than he (Nāḍījaṅgha) 3. 191. 9-14. [See Rājadharman]
निमिष: Nimiṣa m.: A mythical bird, living in the world of Suparṇas 5. 99. 10, 1. Born in the कुल of Vainateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; living on serpents; marked with श्रीवत्स, his deity is Viṣṇu; by action a Kṣatriya, not obtaining Brahmin-hood because responsible for destroying his kinsmen 5. 99. 2-8.
निमेष: Nimeṣa1 m.: A mythical bird, living in the world of Suparṇas 5. 99. 10, 1. Born in the कुल of Vianateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; living on serpents; marked with श्रीवत्स, his deity is Viṣṇu; by action a Kṣatriya, not obtaining Brahminhood because responsible for destroying his kins-men 5. 99. 2-8.

Nimeṣa2 m.: A mythical bird (पक्षिन्) ? He fought with Garuḍa while the latter was on his expedition to fetch अमृत; Garuḍa tore him apart with his wings, nails and beak 1. 28. 19-20 [According to Nīlakaṇṭha Nimeṣa was the name of a Yakṣa, cf. his remark on 1. 32. 18 Bom. Ed.]
निशाकर: Niśākara m.: A mythical bird, living in the world of Suparṇas 5. 99, 14, 1. Born in the कुल of Vainateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; living on serpents, marked with श्रीवत्स, his deity is Viṣṇu; by action a Kṣatriya, not obtaining Brahminhood because responsible for destroying his kinsmen 5. 99. 2-8.
निष्ट्यूनक: Niṣṭyūnaka m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 9, 2.
निष्ठूरिक: Niṣṭhūrika m.: A mythical serpent; living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 12, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7.
नील: Nīla1 m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, listed among her sons by Sūta at the request of Śaunaka 1. 31. 7, 2.

Nīla2 m.: A monkey-chief. One of the guardians of the army of mon-keys when it proceeded towards the southern ocean 3. 267. 19, 21; he smashed with a big rock Pramāthin, younger brother of Dūṣaṇa, when Pramāthin attacked Lakṣmaṇa 3. 271. 25, 19-23; Nīla, with other monkey-chiefs, kept watch over the bodies of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa when they fell on the ground and were bound by the arrows of Indrajit 3. 273. 1-4; he, and other monkey-chiefs, applied the water sent by Kubera to their eyes so that they could see the invisible beings 3. 273. 9-13; he and other monkey-chiefs surrounded Rāvaṇa when he rushed against Rāma 3. 274. 3.

Nīla m.: Name of a mountain. A. Location: Listed among the six mountains lying to the north of the Bhārata-varṣa (6. 7. 6) and which extend from the west to the east and are submerged in the eastern and the western oceans at the two ends 6. 7. 2 (for citation see Niṣadha); these six moun-tains lie at a distance of hundreds of योजनस् from one another 6. 7. 4; to the south of the Nīla and to the north of the Niṣadha there is the big, eternal Jambū tree named Sudarśana 6. 8. 18; the Śvetavarṣa lies beyond the Nīla mountain 6. 7. 35; the Ramaṇakavarṣa lies to the south of the Śvetavarṣa and to the north of the Nīla 6. 9. 2; to south of the Nīla and to the north of the Meru lie the Uttarakurus 6. 8. 2; to the south of the Nīla and to the north of the Niṣadha lies the mountain Mālyavant 6. 7. 7. B. Description: Big (महागिरि) 3. 186. 103; reckoned by Brahman among the kings of mountains (एते पर्वतराजानः) 14. 43. 5; all the six mountains are frequented by the Siddhas and the Cāraṇas (सिद्धचारणसेविताः) 6. 7. 4. C. Characteristics: All the six mountains are full of jewels (षड् एते रत्नपर्वताः) 6. 7. 2; the Nīla is full of the cat's eye gems (वैडूर्यमय) 6. 7. 3; the Brahmanical seers live there (नीले ब्रह्मर्षयो नृप) 6. 7. 49; listed by Brahman among the mountains which are characterized by the middle quality i. e. the quality of रजस् (मध्यमो गुणः) 14. 43. 1; (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 14. 43. 1: मध्यमो गुणः रजोगुणप्रधानः) 14. 43. 4. D. Past event: One of the mountains seen by Mārkaṇḍeya in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 = Nārāyaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 103; E. Importance: Finds place in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 26, 2.

Nīla nt.: Name of a Varṣa. One of the seven Varṣas of the Jambu-dvīpa; beyond Nīla lay the Śvetavarṣa (नीलात् परतरं श्वेतम्) 6. 7. 35; in these Varṣas, people in each succeeding one excelled those in the preceding one in duration of life, health, as well as in धर्म, काम, and अर्थ; in these Varṣas, people lived in harmony with one another 6. 7. 37-38 (for citation see Airāvata).
नर्तन: Nartana nt.: Name of a missile (अस्त्र). One of the eight missiles known to Arjuna; enumerated by Rāma Jāmadagnya for the information of Duryodhana 5. 94. 3 [for the effects produced by it on the enemy see Akṣisaṃtarjana].
नाक: Nāka nt.: Name of a missile (अस्त्र). One of the eight missiles known to Arjuna, enumerated by Rāma Jāmadagnya for the information of Duryodhana 5. 94. 38 [For the effects produced by it on the enemy see Akṣisaṃtarjana].
नाग: Nāga astra nt.: Name of a missile. It was employed repeatedly by Arjuna to tie the feet of the army of the Saṃśap-takas and render them motionless (पद-बन्धं ततश् चक्रे … नागं अस्त्रं महाराज संप्रोदीर्य मुहुर् मुहुः ॥ यान् उद्दिश्य रणे पार्थः पदबन्धं चकार ह । ते बद्धाः पदबन्धेन पाण्डवेन महात्मना । निश्चेष्टा अभवन्) 8. 37. 21, 22; it was rendered useless by Suśarman by employing Sauparṇa astra 8. 37. 25-27 (बभौ बलं तद् विमुक्तं पदबन्धात्).
नारायणास्त्र: Nārāyaṇāstra nt.: Name of the missile employed unsuccessfully by Aśvatthāman, after the death of his father Droṇa, to kill the Pāṇḍavas 1. 1. 145; 1. 2. 165; 7. 166. 55; a sub-पर्वन् related to the employment of the Nārāyaṇāstra occurs after the sub-पर्वन् related to द्रोणवध 1. 2. 58. A. History: Droṇa received the Nārā-yaṇāstra as a boon from Nārāyaṇa himself who appeared before him in the form of a Brāhmaṇa 7. 166. 43-44, 51; with its acquisition Droṇa became unrivalled in battle 7. 166. 45; given by Nārāyaṇa also to Aśvatthāman 7. 166. 50; Aśva-tthāman knew how to release it (सकल्यम् for सकल्पम् ? See Cr. Notes 7, p. 1157 on 166. 42; Nī. कल्यः प्रयोगः on Bom. Ed. 7. 195. 30), and how to withdraw it (सनिवर्तनम्) 7. 166. 42 (but See Section C. 3 below); Nārāyaṇāstra known only to Droṇa and Aśvatthāman; it was not known even to Arjuna and the other Pāṇḍavas, nor to Kṛṣṇa, Sātyaki, Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin 7. 166. 2. 41-42. B. Descrip-tion: heavenly (दिव्य) 1. 1. 145; 7. 166. 60; great missile (महास्त्र) 7. 166. 49; (परम) 7. 166. 44; fierce, frightful (उग्र) 1. 2. 165; (घोररूपं भयावहम्) 7. 167. 6. C. Use: (1) To be used with great circumspection: The missile was not to be employed in haste (न त्व् इदं सहसा ब्रह्मन् प्रयोक्तव्यं कथंचन); since it did not return without killing the enemy, it might kill, if used without circumspection, even one who did not deserve to be killed 7. 166. 46-47; (2) Mode of release: To use it, Aśvatthāman touched water and produced the divine missile (तथोक्त्वा द्रोणपुत्रो ऽपि तदोपस्पृश्य भारत । प्रादुश्चकार तद् दिव्यम् अस्त्रं नारायणं तदा) 7. 166. 60; (3) Restrictions: It could be used only once, and it could not be withdrawn; hence Aśvatthāman unable to employ it again when requested by Duryodhana to do so; if with-drawn the अस्त्र would kill the user 7. 171. 24, 27, 28, 30. D. Effects: When em-ployed, the missile released powerful arrows (? कृशाश्वतनयाः), as also sharp arrows which would fill the directions 7. 166. 38; it let loose many heavenly weapons (दिव्यानि शस्त्रवर्षाणि) and the employer (Aśvat-thāman) shone with lustre 7. 166. 50; the arrows released from it would hit the enemies as desired by the employer (Aśvatthāman); it would release rocks at will and iron-tipped arrows which would put the enemy to flight 7. 166. 53-54; when Aśvatthāman produced the missile, thunderous winds carrying water-drops blew in cloud-less sky, the earth shook, and the ocean was agitated; rivers started flowing in the opposite direction; peaks of mountains were shattered; sun became turbid (कलुष), and the gods, the demons, and the Gandharvas were frightened 7. 167. 1-5; arrows with shining tips appeared in thou-sands to cover the army of the enemy and fill the directions; (hot) iron balls (कार्ष्णाय-समया गुडाः) shining like celestial bodies, शतघ्नीस् (‘hundred-killers’), fire-arms (? हुताशदाः), and disks with sharp ends (चक्राणि क्षुरान्तानि), all these were produc-ed by the Nārāyaṇāstra (7. 170. 16-19); as the Pāṇḍava warriors tried to resist the missile, it grew in strength 7. 170. 21; as a result, the Pāṇḍava army was burnt and destroyed 7. 170. 22-23; to combat it successfully Kṛṣṇa advised the warriors to lay down arms and get down from their chariots and mounts 7. 170. 38-42; when all followed his in-struction, Bhīma wanted to resist the missile with arrows, mace, and the strength of his arms; as a consequence, the Nārāyaṇāstra grew in strength; since other warriors had laid down their arms the missile des-cended on Bhīma with all its strength 7. 170. 45-46, 50-51, 57-60; seeing Bhīma surrounded by the Nārāyaṇāstra, Arjuna tried to protect him from the missile by using Vāruṇāstra; since this was of no avail, Arjuna and Vāsudeva left from their chariot, ran to Bhīma, and entered through the cover of lustre produced by the अस्त्र; since they had no weapons, the अस्त्र did not affect them (and also because of the effect of the Vāru-ṇāstra and the prowess of Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna); Bhīma was forced down by Nara (Arjuna) and Nārāyaṇa (Kṛṣṇa) from his chariot and forced to give up weapons; the Nārāyaṇāstra was then pacified; the quarters became clear and gentle winds blew; the birds and the animals felt assured 7. 171. 1, 3, 6, 10-14, 20-22; if Vāsudeva had not shown the way to combat the Nārāyaṇāstra it would have meant death for the enemy (of the Kauravas) 7. 171. 28; but the missile was rendered in-effective and the Pāṇḍavas freed from it 7. 171. 33; 8. 1. 42. E. The means to pacify the Nārāyaṇāstra: When released, the missile must kill the enemy and only then it would subside; the other ways of pacifying it were to run away from it, to lay down the arms, to beg for life, and ask refuge (वधः संख्ये द्रवश् चैव शस्त्राणां च विसर्जनम् । प्रयाचनं च शत्रूणां गमनं शर-णस्य च ॥ एते प्रशमने योगा महास्त्रस्य परन्तप) 7. 166. 48-49. F. Status: The Pāśupatāstra of Śiva rated superior to the Nārāyaṇāstra 13. 14. 127.
निवृत्त: Nivṛtta nt.: One of the twenty-one movements (सो ऽचरद् विविधान् मार्गान्) used while fighting with a sword and a shield. Dhṛṣṭadyumna used it when he, with a sword and a shield in hand, wanted to attack Droṇa who was shooting arrows at him 7. 164. 145-148.
नकुलाख्यान: Nakulākhyāna nt.: Name of an आख्यान mentioned in the list of the contents of the Āśvamedhikaparvan 1. 2. 209. The incident which occurred at the conclusion of the Aśvamedha sacrifice of Yudhiṣṭhira is narrated in the अध्यायस् 14. 92-96.
नलोपाख्यान: Nalopākhyāna nt.: Name of an उपा-ख्यान mentioned in the list of the contents of the Āraṇyakaparvan 1. 2. 109. Described as most pious (धर्मिष्ठ) and which causes the rise of compassion (in the hearer) (करुणोदय); here is described the condition of Damayantī when Nala was overpowered by calamity (दमयन्त्याः स्थितिर् यत्र नलस्य व्यसनागमे) 1. 2. 109; the उपाख्यान is narrated in the अध्यायस् 3. 50-78.
नारदागमन: Nāradāgamana nt.: Name of the 95th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 67. The incident is mentioned in the narra-tion of the contents of the Āśramavāsa-parvan; Nārada came to visit Yudhiṣṭhira and told him about the great destruction of the Viṛṣṇis 1. 2. 217; (Actually Nārada re-ported to Yudhiṣṭhira about the death of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gāndhārī and Kuntī in the forest-fire (15. 45. 9-38); it was Dāruka who reported to the Pāṇḍavas about the destruc-tion of the Vṛṣṇis 16. 6. 1); the पर्वन् is related to the अध्यायस् 15. 45-47.
नारायणास्त्रस्य: Nārāyaṇāstrasya mokṣaḥ: Name of the 72nd पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃ-graha 1. 2. 58 (मोक्षो नारायणास्त्रस्य पर्वानन्तरम् उच्यते). The incident of the release of the Nārāyaṇāstra by Aśvatthāman, enraged at the death of his father Droṇa, is mentioned in the narration of the contents of the Droṇaparvan 1. 2. 165, and in Dhṛtarāṣṭra's summary of the events made for Saṃjaya 1. 1. 145; the पर्वन् is related to the अध्यायस् 7. 166-173.
नारायणीय: Nārāyaṇīya nt., Nārāyaṇakathā f.: Name of an आख्यान 12. 334. 12, or of a कथा 12. 327. 4; 12. 331. 7, 19; it comprises the अध्यायस् 12. 321-337. A. Characterizations: This section (or its parts) generally referred to as आख्यान 12. 326. 113; 12. 331. 1; 12. 326. 121 (आख्यानवर, also 12. 337. 16); 12. 334. 2 (भगवदाख्यान); 12. 334. 11 (महदाख्यान), or as कथा 12. 326. 118; 12. 326. 115 (कथामृत) 12. 331. 4 (कथामृत) 12. 334. 4; 12. 335. 6; but occasionally also as पूराण 12. 326. 112; 12. 329. 2; or पुराण equal to Veda (in import-ance) (पुराणं वेदसंमितम्) 12. 326. 106; as old इतिहास (इतिहासं पुरातनम्) 12. 321. 7; as धर्मसंहिता 12. 327. 4; as ब्रह्म 12. 326. 107; as a great उप-निषद्(अ), together with the four Vedas, com-posed by Nārāyaṇa (इदं महोपम्षदं चतुर्वेदसमन्वितम् … नारायणमुखोद्-गीतम्) 12. 326. 100-101; as ज्ञान pertain-ing to all the three times (past, present and future) which dawned on Vyāsa by the favour of Nārāyaṇa (नारायणप्रसादेन … त्रैकालि-कम् इदं ज्ञानं प्रादुर्भूतम्) 12. 327. 22-23, 97; as सात्वत धर्म 12. 336. 78, (51), or simply as धर्म 12. 336. 9 ff. B. Description: The आख्यान (or its parts) described as great (महत्) 12. 334. 11, very great (सुमहत्) 12. 331. 1; best (उत्तम) 12. 337. 16, unparalleled (अनु-त्तम) 12. 331. 4; difficult to be understood (गहन) 12. 321. 6; pious (पुण्या) 12. 335. 6; destroying all sins (सर्वपाप-प्रणाशनी) 12. 331. 8; proceeding directly from the mouth of Nārāyaṇa (नारायन-मुखोद्गीत) 12. 326. 101; originating from the Ṛṣi (Nārāyaṇa) and transmitted by tradition (आर्षेयम् पारंपर्यागतम्) 12. 326. 113; related to the origin of Ṛṣi (Vyāsa from Nārāyaṇa) (आर्षेय) 12. 337. 16; of great importance as a prayer to be muttered (परमं जप्यम्) 12. 326. 123; based on the Nārāyaṇakathā (नारायणकथाश्रय) 12. 331. 4; churned out of the Bhāratā-khyāna of a hundred thousand stanzas (as butter from curds etc.) 12. 331. 2-4; 12. 326. 115; essence of all the hundreds of religious उपाख्यानस् heard by Yudhiṣṭhira from Bhīṣma 12. 326. 114. C. Glorifica-tion and importance: Contains a स्तोत्र of Bhagavān (12. 326. 1) who is विश्व, निर्गुण and महात्मन् 12. 325. 3; constitutes the praise of the high-souled excellent Puruṣa (महात्मनः पुरुषवरस्य कीर्तनम्) 12. 327. 107; and describes the greatness of the Paramātman (माहात्म्यं परमात्मनः) 12. 334. 8; neither a visit to all the आश्रमस् nor bathing in all the तीर्थस् yields as much fruit as does the Nārāyaṇakathā 12. 331. 7; it has the purifying effect on listeners (पावितात्माद्य संवृत्वः श्रुत्वेमाम् आदितः कथाम् 12. 334. 4; पाविताः स्म त्वया ब्रह्मन् पुण्यां कथयता कथाम् 12. 335. 6); it should not be narrated to one who is not devoted to Vāsudeva 12. 326. 113. D. Nature and form: It is a glorification of Nārāyaṇa in different contexts and is in many places in the form of dialogues (1) between Nārāyaṇa and Nārada in the Badaryāśrama 12. 321. 23-43; 12. 331. 20-32; 12. 332. 1-23; 12. 333. 2-25 (11-25 speakers Nara and Nārāyaṇa); at the Śvetadvīpa 12. 326. 10-98; (2) Bhagavān and Arjuna अध्य्स्। 12. 328-330; (3) Vyāsa and Vaiśaṃpāyana 12. 327. 20-98; 12. 337. 15. 57; (4) Bhīṣma and Yudhiṣṭhira 12. 322. 13-52; 12. 323. 1-57; 12. 324. 1-39; 12. 326. 102-120; (5) Vaiśaṃpāyana and Jana-mejaya 12. 327. 1-19; 99-101; 12. 336-337. E. Etymologies: Arjuna requested Bhaga-van to tell him etymologies of his names based on qualities and activities (निरुक्तं गुणकर्मजम् 12. 328. 3, 10; 12. 328. 6-7 (यानि नामानि ते देव कीर्तितानि महर्षि-भिः । … तेषां निरुक्तम् त्वत्तोऽहं स्रोतुम् इच्छामि केशव); also 12. 328. 1-4; Bhaga-vān then explained these etymologies to Arjuna 12. 328. 8-51; 12. 330. 1-31. F. Narrations: Various portions of this आख्यान are narrated (1) (उपनिषद) by Nārāyaṇa himself to Nārada 12. 326. 100-101 (इदं महपनिषदम् … पञ्चरात्रा-नुशब्दितम् ॥ नारायणमुखोद्गीतम्); Nārada narrated it to Brahman 12. 326. 101-102, from whom it passed on successively to the Siddhas, Sūrya, 66000 ऋषिस्, gods द्विज Asita manes (पितृस्) (including Śaṃtanu); from Śaṃtanu it went to Bhīṣma and then to Yudhiṣṭhira 12. 326. 105-111; (2) (धर्म) narrated by Nārāyaṇa himself to Narada 12. 336. 50, and then by Nārada to Pārtha (Yudhiṣṭhira) in the presence of the sages (including Vyāsa), and within the hearing of Kṛṣṇa and Bhīṣma 12. 336. 11 (or by Nārada to Vyāsa and then by Vyāsa to Yudhiṣṭhira, the sages, Kṛṣṇa and Bhīṣma 12. 336. 59-60), and also by Vyāsa to Vaiśaṃpāyana and then by the latter to Janamejaya 12. 336. 12, 57, 80; (3) (आख्यान) narrated by Nārada to Vyāsa seated among the sages, and to the Pāṇḍavas within the hearing of Kṛṣṇa and Bhīṣma 12. 334. 12, and further by Vyāsa to Vaiśaṃpāyana and by the latter to Janamejaya 12. 334. 8, 12; 12. 331. 19 (नारायणकथा); (4) (ज्ञान) Vyāsa narrated the ज्ञान which dawned on him by the favour of Nārāyaṇa to his pupils Vaiśaṃpāyana and others, and to Śuka 12. 327. 15-23, 97, 99, 101, and then Vaiśaṃ-pāyana to Janamejaya 12. 327 15, 19, 101. G. स्रवणफल: (of the आख्यान or the कथा) One who always recites this आख्यान or listens to it, being devoted to one object, and very attentively, in a secluded place (एकान्तभावोपगत एकान्ते सुसमाहितः), reaches the Śvetadvīpa and, having obtained the lustre of the moon, would no doubt enter the god of thousand flames (स सहस्रार्-चिषम् देवं प्रविशेन् नात्र संशयः) 12. 326. 116-17; (12. 327. 6); it one, afflicted (by diseases) listens to this कथा from the beginning, he will be freed from the disease; one who listens to it out of curiosity (जिज्ञासुः) obtains his desires, and a devotee (after death) would go along the course of a devotee (भक्तो भक्तगतिं व्रजेत्) 12. 326. 118; (of the ज्ञान expounded by Vyāsa) one who listens to it or one who recites it, having bowed down to Bhagavān and with attentive mind, is freed from disease, becomes lustrous, and gets strength and good complexion; one who is suffering from illness is freed of illness, one held in captivity is released from bonds, one who entertains desires obtains them and long life; a Brāhmaṇa thereby knows all, a Kṣatriya is victorious, a Vaiśya obtains much profit and a Śūdra becomes happy; one who is devoid of a son has a son; a maiden gets the cherished husband, the woman who experiences difficulty in delivery delivers easily (लग्नगर्भा विमुच्यते), a pregnant woman delivers a son, a barren woman has abundant progeny consisting of sons and grandsons; one who recites this while on journey reaches his destination safely; (in short) whatever desire a person entertains that he definitely gets; this is the considered assurance of the great sage (इदं महर्षेर् वचनं विनिश्-चितम्) that by listening to the praise of the Excellent Person (पुरुषवर) the devotees are very comfortable (निशम्य भक्ताः सु-सुखं लभन्ते) 12. 327. 102-107. H. End: After listening to this great Nārāyaṇīya आख्यान, king Janamejaya resumed all the rites necessary for the completion of the (snake) sacrifice (एतद् तु महद् आख्यानं श्रुत्वा पारिक्षितो नृपः । ततो यज्ञसमा-प्त्यर्थं क्रियाः सर्वाः समारभत् ॥ 12. 334. 11). [See Puruṣasukta, Hayaśiras]
निरुक्त: Nirukta nt.: Name of the text dealing with etymologies. The sage Yāska is credited to have rescued by the favour of Kṛṣṇa the lost Nirukta when he praised Kṛṣṇa as शिपिविष्ट 12. 330. 8 (स्तुत्वा मां शिपिविष्टेति यास्को मुनिर् उदारधीः । मत्प्रसादाद् अधो नष्टं निरुक्तम् अभिजग्मिवान्; Nī. अधो नष्टं वेदहरणवेलायां पाताले ऽन्तर्हि-तम् on Bom. Ed. 12. 342. 73); those who know the Nirukta (name of the text ?) and the Veda praise Kṛṣṇa as Adhokṣaja in the ritual context 12. 330. 18 (निरुक्तम् वेद-विदुषो … ते मां गायन्ति प्राग्वंशे अधो-क्षज इति स्थितिः; Nī. प्राग्वंशे यज्ञशा-लैकदेशे on Bom. Ed. 12. 342. 83); gods long for him who knows the Vedas, the Vedāṅgas (?), the whole sacrificial proce-dure, the Nirukta (text ?), and the highest truth to be in the शरीरात्मन् (वेदांश् च वेद्यं च विधिं च कृत्स्नम् अथो निरुक्तं परमार्थतां च । सर्वं शरीरात्मनि यः प्रवेद तस्मै स्म देवाः स्पृहय-न्ति नित्यम् 12. 237. 30; but Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 245. 30: वेद्यं वियदादि, विधिं कर्मकाण्डम्, निरुक्तं शब्दैकगम्यं परलोकादि परमार्थताम् सत्यस्वभाव-तां चात्मनः); Bṛhaspati told Prajāpati that even after studying the Vedas and the other texts like the Nirukta and the Vyākaraṇa he does not know the ultimate source of beings (भूतप्रकृतिं न वेद्मि) 12. 194. 8; the Nirukta (personified, among other personified texts) came to the sacrifice of Rudra who had assumed the form of Varuṇa 13. 85. 5, 2, 7-8.
निर्याण: Niryāṇa nt.: Name of the 56th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 52, 33, 70. Referred to as marching out of the chariots, the horses, the footsoldiers, and the elephants from the city Hāstinapura and the mention of their total count (बलसंख्या-नम्) while listing the contents of the Udyogaparvan 1. 2. 149; related to the अध्यायस् 5. 149-152 (अभिनिर्याणपर्वन्).
नैघण्टुक: Naighaṇṭuka nt.: Name of a text giving synonyms (?). Supposed to have been composed by Prajāpati Kaśyapa 12. 330. 24; in it Kṛṣṇa is called Vṛṣākapi (because Vṛṣa is Dharma and कपि means ‘the best, the highest’; Vṛṣākapi thus means ‘the highest Dharma’) 12. 330. 23-24.
नन्दन: Nandana nt.: Name of Indra's celestial garden. A. Relationship with deities: (1) Mostly  related to Indra 3. 44. 3; 3. 78. 3; 3. 164. 41; 5. 11. 9-10; (2) Once with Aśvinau 14. 15. 4. B. Description: Heavenly (दिव्य) 3. 44. 3; garden of the gods (देवो-द्यान) 3. 247. 8-9; holy (पुण्य) 3. 247. 9; offering sporting grounds for the righteous (विहाराः पुण्यकर्मणाम्) 3. 247. 9; resort-ed to by the hosts of Apsarases (अप्सरोगण-सेवित) 3. 44. 3; for the relationship of the Apsarases with the Nandanavana also cf. 1. 84. 17; 13. 26. 42; 13. 63. 17; house of the Gandharvas and the Apsarases (गन्-धर्वाणाम् अप्सरसां च सद्म) 13. 105. 23; liked by the king of the Kiṃnaras (किं-नरराजजुष्ट) 13. 105. 23; liked by Nārada (प्रियं वनं नन्दनं नारदस्य) 13. 105. 23; full of flowers (सुपुष्पित) 13. 105. 23; the trees in the Nandana have a holy fragrance, are full of flowers and have pleas-ing forms (पुण्यगन्धान् पश्यन्न् अगान् पुष्पितांश् चारुरूपान्) 1. 84. 17; as though inviting (the visitors) with trees having heavenly flowers (दिव्यकुसुमैर् आह्वयद्-भिर् इव द्रुमैः) 3. 44. 3; it is cherished by those who are skilled in dancing and singing and who offer unsolicited company (ये नृत्तगीतकुशला जनाः सदा ह्य् अयाचमानाः सहिताश् चरन्ति । तथाविधानाम् एष लोकः) 13. 105. 24; for the description of a forest which is compared with Nandana cf. 12. 163. 6-10. C. Epic events: (1) When Arjuna reached the Amarāvatī of Indra he saw there the Nandanavana 3. 44. 3; (2) Mātali, on way to Indra's Amarā-vatī, showed Nandana to Arjuna 3. 164. 41. D. Past and mythological events: (1) Aṣṭaka asked Yayāti why he fell down on earth from the Nandana where he had lived for an अयुत of centuries (संवत्सराणाम् अयुतं शतानाम्) 1. 85. 1; Yayāti told him that he lived in the Nandana for an अयुत of centuries in the company of the Apsarases, but when his merit was exhausted (क्षीणपुण्यः) he fell down on earth from the Nandana 1. 84. 17, 19; (2) When Nahuṣa became the king of heaven he sported in all the heavenly gardens and in the groves of the Nandana (देवोद्यानेषु सर्वेषु नन्दनोपवनेषु च) 5. 11. 9-10; (3) The Devadūta while describing to Mudgala the heavenly worlds reached by the highly meritorious persons told him that there were in those worlds heavenly gardens, the Nandana and the rest; these offered sporting grounds to the righteous (नन्दनादीनि पुण्यानि विहाराः पुण्यकर्मणाम्) 3. 247. 9; (4) Gautama wanted king Dhṛtarāṣṭra to give back to him his elephant for which he was offered in return stay in the Nandana (वनं नन्दनम् । … तत्र त्वाहम् हस्ति-नं यातयिष्ये) 13. 105. 23 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 102. 14: यातयिष्ये हस्तिनं स्वीयं फलं त्वत्तो ग्रहीष्य इत्य् अर्थः); (5) The mother of Viśvarūpa approached to intercede on behalf of the Asuras her son who was in the Nandana garden (Viśvarūpa used to offer shares directly to gods but indirectly to Asuras) 12. 329. 19. E. Mentioned as reward for meritorious acts: (1) By resorting to the rivers Nandā and Mahānandā one who is controlled and causes no injury to others (दान्तः … अहिंसकः) is waited upon by the Apsarases in the Nandana 13. 26. 42; (2) By giving as gift a bull and fragrant substances under the coustella-tion Citrā (चित्रायाम् ऋषभं दत्त्वा पुण्यान् गन्धांश् च) one enjoys stay in the Nan-dana 13. 63. 17; (3) One who recites the आख्यान of women's duties towards their hus-band (पतिधर्म), narrated by Śāṇḍilī to Sumanā of the Kekayas, on every पर्वन् day reaches the Devaloka (after death) and lives happily in the Nandana 13. 124. 22. F. Similes: (1) Forests and similar places compared with the Nandana: (i) King Duḥṣanta, when out for hunting, saw a garden like the Nandana 1. 63. 12; also 1. 64. 28; (ii) Brāhmaṇa Gautama reached a forest like the Nandana 12. 163. 7; (iii) The forest on the Gandhamādana mountain compared with the Nandana 3. 155. 36; (iv) Rāvaṇa kept Sītā near the garden of the Aśoka trees which was like the Nandana (नन्दनोपमे । अशोकवनिकाभ्याशे) 3. 264. 41; (v) The Pāṇḍavas on seeing the region of the lotus pond (Nalinī) of Kubera were happy as are the Brahmanical seers when they come to live in the Nandana 3. 174. 10; (2) Towns and similar places: (i) Nala, with Damayantī, lived in his town like Indra in his Nandana 3. 78. 3; (ii) When the war was over Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna enjoyed themselves in different places as do the Aśvinau in the Nandana 14. 15. 4.
नन्दा: Nandā f.: Name of a river. A. Location: In the east (1. 207. 5; 3. 85. 3; 3. 91. 28), on the top of the mountain Kuṇḍoda (नन्दा च गिरिमूर्-धनि) 3. 85. 20-21; on the Hemakūṭa 3. 109. 1-2, i. e. on the Ṛṣabhakūṭa 3. 109. 7. B. Description: One that destroys the fear of sin (पापभयापहा) 3. 109. 1. C. Epic events: (1) During the term of exile Arjuna, while going to the east, saw the river Nandā among many other rivers 1. 207. 7; (2) While in forest, Yudhiṣṭhira with his followers visited it 3. 109. 1; Lomaśa asked Yudhiṣṭhira to bathe with his brothers in the river Nandā (अभिषेकं वै तस्मात् कुरु सहानुजः । ततो नन्दाप्लुताङ्गस् त्वम्) and then proceed to the river Kauśikī; accordingly Yudhiṣṭhira and his followers (सगणः) took bath in the Nandā 3. 109. 18-20. D. Mythological event: Once gods visited the Nandā and the people rushed to see them; not wishing to be seen by the people Indra and other gods made the region inaccessible 3. 109. 11-12. E. Reward: (1) Bathing in the Nandā destroys sin instantly (सद्यः पाप्मा निहन्यते) 3. 109. 18; (2) By visiting the Nandā even once (सकृत् नन्दां समासाद्य) the soul of a Brāhmaṇa is disciplined (कृतात्मा भवति द्विजः) and, freed of sins, he goes to the world of Śakra 3. 82. 138; (3) By visiting the Nandā one who is controlled (दान्तः) and who does not cause injury to others (अहिंसकः) is waited upon by the Apsarases in the Nandana 13. 26. 42. F. Importance: Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 23, 2.
नर्मदा: Narmadā f.: Name of a river. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 13; in the south, to the south of the river Carmaṇvatī 2. 28. 1, 7-8; in the west, it flows westwards through the Avanti country 3. 87. 1, 2. B. Description: Holy (पुण्या) 3. 87. 2; 13. 2. 18; auspicious (शिवा) 13. 2. 18; river of the gods (देवनदी) 13. 2. 18; excellent among the rivers (सरितां वरा) 15. 26. 13; great river (महानदी) 3. 121. 15; 12. 52. 32; famous in the three worlds (त्रैलोक्यविश्रुता) 3. 80. 71; its water is cool (शीतजला) 13. 2. 18; flowing westwards (प्रत्यक्स्रोता) 3. 87. 2; it has on its banks Priyaṅgu and mango trees (प्रियङ्ग्वाम्रवनोपेता) and has garlands of abundant canes (वानीरवन-मालिनी) 3. 87. 2. C. Epic events: (1) Sahadeva in his expedition to the south (2. 28. 1) reached the Narmadā where he defeated the two Avanti princes Vinda and Anuvinda 2. 28. 9; (2) From the river Payoṣṇī, Yudhiṣṭhira and his brothers went to the mountain Vaiḍūrya and the river Narmadā 3. 121. 15. D. Past and Mytho-logical events: (1) The river Narmadā fell in love with Duryodhana, son of Durjaya (13. 2. 12) and gave birth to a daughter Sudarśanā 13. 2. 18-19; (2) The river Narmadā became the wife of king Purukutsa 15. 26. 13; (3) Narmadā was one of the rivers seen by the sage Mārkaṇḍeya in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 = Nārāyaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 94. E. Importance: (1) In the region of the river Narmadā and the mountain Vaiḍūrya (3. 121. 15, 18) there is the lake of Cyavana 3. 122. 1, 5; 3. 125. 11 (see *Cyavanasya saras); (2) The river Narmadā is one of the rivers which are descri-bed as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 13, 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā); (3) Listed by Mārkaṇḍeya among the rivers known as mothers of the fire-hearths (i. e. on the banks of which sacrifices were performed; (for citation and Nī. see Kapilā) 3. 212. 23-24; (4) Narmadā is one of the rivers which in bodily form (देहवन्तः) wait upon Varuṇa in his Sabhā 2. 9. 18, 21; (5) The meeting point between the river Narmadā and the mountain Vaiḍūrya is looked upon as the joint between the Tretā and the Dvāpara Yugas 3. 121. 18-19; (6) Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 15, 2. F. Holiness: (1) By giving offerings to manes and gods on the river Narmadā one gets the fruit of an Agni-ṣṭoma sacrifice 3. 80. 71; (2) By bathing (उपस्पृश्य) at the source of the Narmadā (नर्मदायाश् च प्रभवे) one gets the fruit of performing a horse sacrifice 3. 83. 9; (3) One who bathes (अवतीर्य) in the Narmadā obtains the worlds of gods and (meritorious) kings (देवानाम् एति कौन्तेय तथा राज्ञां सलोकताम्) 3. 121. 18; (4) By bathing (उपस्पृश्य) in the Narmadā and by fasting there for a fortnight one becomes a prince (in the next birth ?) (एकपक्षं निराहारो राजपुत्रो विधीयते) 13. 26. 47; G. Simile: The army of the Pāṇḍavas moving in two parts compared with the river Narmadā flowing in two streams (see Ṛkṣavant) 12. 52. 32.
नलिनी: Nalinī1 f.: Name of a river. One of the seven streams into which the Gaṅgā was divided at the lake Bindusaras where the river was first established after her fall from the Brahmaloka (तत्र त्रिपथगा देवी … सप्तधा प्रतिपद्यते 6. 7. 41, 44) is called Nalinī 6. 7. 45; one of the rivers seen by the sage Mārkaṇḍeya in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 = Nārāyaṇa 6. 187. 3) 3. 186. 94.

Nalinī2 f.: Name (?) of the lotus pond of Kubera. A. Location: In the north (उदीच्यां दिशि) 7. 57. 23; on the summit of the Kailāsa, in an auspicious and beautiful forest (कैलासशिखरे रम्ये ददर्श शुभकानने) 3. 151. 1; near the residence of Kubera (कुबेरभवनाभ्याशे) 3. 151. 2; in the sporting place of Kubera (कुबे-रस्य विहारे) 7. 57. 23; it could be seen from the Badarī, the place of residence of Nārāyaṇa 3. 174. 8-9. B. Description: Auspicious (शुभा) and purifying the world (पवित्रभूतां लोकस्य) 3. 151. 3; its water was auspicious (शुभ) and holy (शिव) 3. 151. 4; heavenly (दिव्या) 3. 151. 3, 8; (दिव्यं सरः) 3. 151. 9; pleasing, very pleasing (रम्या) 3. 151. 1, 5; 3. 152. 10; (सुरम्या) 3. 151. 2; (सुमनोहरा) 3. 153. 23; of wonderful appearance (अद्-भुतदर्शना) 3. 151. 3; its ample water was cool, light and clear (शीतं विमलं तोयं … बहु) 3. 151. 4; its water was like nectar (अमृतकल्पम् अम्भः) 3. 152. 22; or was nectar itself (अमृत-रसम्) 3. 151. 4; covered with trees and creepers of different kinds, hence offering ample shade (विपुलच्छायां नानाद्रुमलता-वृताम्) 3. 151. 2; covered with yellow and golden lotuses (हरिताम्बुजसंच्छन्नां … कनकपुष्कराम्) 3. 151. 3; full of golden Saugandhika lotus flowers of excellent fragrance which had variegated and charm-ing stalks of excellent Vaiḍūrya (पद्म-सौगन्धिकायुताम् । जातरूपमयैः पद्-मैश् छन्नां परमगन्धिभिः ॥ वैडूर्-यवरनालैश् च बहुचित्रैर् मनोहरैः) 3. 151. 5-6; full of lotuses, decorated by lotuses (पद्मिनी) 13. 20. 8; (पुष्करिणी) 3. 152. 18, 21; (प्रफुल्लपङ्कजवती) 3. 153. 23; (पद्मभूषिता) 7. 57. 23; sporting ground of Kubera, the king of the Yakṣas (आक्रीडं यक्षराजस्य कुबेरस्य) 3. 151. 7; loved by Kubera (कुबेरकान्ता) 3. 174. 9; highly honoured by the Gandharvas, the Apsa-rases, and gods (गन्धर्वैर् अप्सरोभिश् च देवैश् च परमार्चिताम्) 3. 151. 7; loved by gods and the Siddhas (सुरसिद्धजुष्टा) 3. 174. 9; frequented by sages (सेविताम् ऋषिभिः) 3. 151. 8; guarded by Rākṣasas called the Krodhavaśas under instruction from their king (Kubera) (राक्षसैर् अभिरक्षिताम्) 3. 151. 1; 13. 20. 8; (तच् च क्रोधवशा नाम राक्षसा राजशासनात् । रक्षन्ति) 3. 151. 10; guarded by the Yakṣas, Kiṃpuruṣas, Rākṣasas, Kiṃnaras and by Vaiśravaṇa (Kubera) himself (यक्षैः किंपुरुषैस् तथा । राक्षसैः किंनरैश् चैव गुप्तां वैश्रवणेन च) 3. 151. 8. C. Epic events: (1) Bhīma, in search of the divine Saugandhika flowers (3. 146. 6-14) saw the Nalinī on the summit of the Kailāsa and was very happy to see the lake 3. 151. 1, 9; he invaded the lake for the flowers and, in the encounter that followed, killed over a hundred Rākṣasas near the lotus lake 3. 152. 18; he entered the lake and plucked the Saugandhika flowers 3. 152. 21-22; when the Rākṣasas returned to the lake, after reporting the incident to Kubera, they saw Bhīma sporting in the Nalinī 3. 152. 25; Yudhiṣṭihra and others, helped by Ghaṭotkaca and his Rākṣasas, proceeded towards Kubera's Nalinī 3. 153. 21-22; after meeting Bhīma, they all sported in the Nalinī 3. 153. 28; (reference to Bhīma's invading Kubera's Nalinī for the Mandāra flowers is found in 1. 2. 112); (2) When the Pāṇḍa-vas, on their return journey, saw the Nalinī they became free from grief (नलिनीं विशोकाः संपश्यमानाः) 3. 174. 9; (तां चाथ दृष्ट्वा नलिनीं विशोकाः 3. 174. 10; (3) Arjuna, while proceeding at night to propitiate Śiva to get from him his Pāśupata missile, saw on his way the Nalinī in the sporting ground of Kubera 7. 57. 23. D. Past event: Aṣṭā-vakra saw the Nalinī of Dhanada (Kubera) near the Kailāsa summit of the mountain Himālaya 13. 20. 7. E. Simile: The Pāṇḍavas sported near the Nalinī as do the Brahmanical seers after reaching the Nandana forest 3. 174. 10.
नागधन्वन्: Nāgadhanvan m.: Name of a तीर्थ। Balarāma went along the south bank of the Sarasvatī and reached the Nāga-dhanvan तीर्थ which was not very far from the Dvaitavana (ततः प्रायाद् बलो राजन् दक्षिणेन सरस्वतीम् ॥ गत्वा चैव … नातिदूरं … । धर्मात्मा नागधन्वानं तीर्थं आगमद् अच्युतः ॥ ) 9. 36. 28-29; Vāsuki, the king of the Pannagas, has his abode there and he lives there with many Pannagas (यत्र पन्नगराजस्य वासुकेः संनिवेशनम् । … बहुभिः पन्नगैर् वृतम् ॥ ); gods once assembled there to consecrate, according to the rites (यथा-विधि), Vāsuki as the king of all Pannagas 9. 36. 30-31; one need have no fear from the serpents there (पन्नगेभ्यो भयं तत्र विद्यते न स्म कौरव) 9. 36. 31; there also live perfected sages numbering fourteen thou-sand 9. 36. 30 (ऋषयः सिद्धाः सहस्राणि चतुर्दश); Balarāma gave there to the Brāhmaṇas, according to the rites (विधिवत्), heaps of gems (रत्नसंचयान्) and from there he proceeded towards the east 9. 36. 32.
नागसभ: Nāgasabha m.: Name of a mountain. Pāṇḍu, on his way to the Śataśṛṅga mountain with his two wives, first reached the mountain Nāgasabha 1. 110. 42.
नागोद्भेद: Nāgodbheda m.: Name of a तीर्थ। One of the three तीर्थस् (the other two being the Camasodbheda and the Śivodbheda) where the river Sarasvatī reappears after disappearing at the Vinaśana; by bathing at the Nāgodbheda one goes to the world of the Nāgas 3. 80. 118-119.
नारीतीर्थानि: Nārītīrthāni nt. (pl.): A collective name for the five तीर्थस्। Situated on the coast of the southern ocean (समुद्रे तीर्थानि दक्षिणे) 1. 208. 1; in the marshy land of the southern ocean (दक्षिणे सागरानूपे) 1. 209. 17; as declared by the Brāhmaṇa the five तीर्थस् would become famous as the Nārītīrthas (नारीतीर्थानि नाम्नेह ख्यातिं यास्यन्ति सर्वशः) 1. 209. 11; described as very holy (सुपुण्यानि) 1. 208. 1, holy (पुण्यानि); puri-fying for the thoughtful (पावनानि मनीषि-णाम्) 1. 209. 11, 17; pleasing (रमणियानि) 1. 209. 17; these तीर्थस् are the Agastyatīrtha, the Saubhadra, the Pauloma, the Kāraṃ-dhama and the तीर्थ of Bhāradvāja (भार-द्वाजस्य तीर्थम् 1. 208. 3); they were once adorned by the sages (शोभितानि तपस्विभिः) but were avoided by them due to the fear of the five crocodiles which lived there 1. 208. 1-2, 4-6; Arjuna cleared the तीर्थस् of the crocodiles which were really five Apsarases (तीर्थानि शोधयित्वा) 1. 209. 23; Yudhiṣṭhira, with Draupadī and brothers, later visited these तीर्थस्; he heard there the heroic deed of Arjuna and was pleased; they all bathed in the तीर्थस् and gave thousands of cows as gifts; Yudhiṣṭhira also praised the gift of cows by Arjuna (this gift of Arjuna is not reported earlier) 3. 118. 4-7. (See also the five तीर्थस् named above).
निचीरा: Nicīrā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people use its water for drinking 6. 10. 20, 13; all the rivers listed here are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
निबिड: Nibiḍa m.: Name of a mountain. Mountain of the Krauñcadvīpa; it lay beyond the Govinda mountain 6. 13. 19, 17.
निरृति: Nirṛti m.: Name of a mountain (?). Mentioned in the Tīrthavaṃśa narrated by Aṅgiras 13. 26. 3; described as the mountain of the gods; by visiting it (?) one is freed of the sin of killing a Brāhmaṇa (निरृतिं देवपर्वतम् । … ब्रह्महत्या विशुध्यति) 13. 26. 40.
निश्चीरा: Niścīrā f.: Name of a river. Famous in the three worlds (त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुताम्) 3. 82. 119; by visiting (समासाद्य) the river Niścīrā one gets the fruit of a horse sacrifice and goes to the world of Viṣṇu; those who give gift at the confluence of the Niścīrā (निश्चीरासंगमे) go without doubt to the world of Brahman; on this river is situated the hermitage of Vasiṣṭha 3. 82. 119-121.
निषध: Niṣadha m.: Name of a mountain. A. Location: Listed among the six mountains lying to the north of the Bhārata-varṣa (6. 7. 6) and which extend from the west to the east and are merged in the eastern and the western oceans at the two ends (प्रागायता महाराज षड् एते … । अवगाढा ह्य् उभ-यतः समुद्रौ पूर्वपश्चिमौ ॥ ) 6. 7. 2; these mountains lie at a distance of hundreds of योजनस् from one another (तेषाम् अन्तर-विष्कम्भो योजनानि सहस्रशः) 6. 7. 4; to the south of the Nīla mountain and to the north of the Niṣadha there is the big, eternal Jambū tree named Sudarśana (दक्षिणेन तु नीलस्य निषधस्योत्तरेण तु । सुदर्शनो नाम महाञ् जम्बूवृक्षः सनातनः) 6. 8. 18; to the south of the Nīla mountain and to the north of the Niṣadha also lies the mountain Mālyavant 6. 7. 7. B. Description: Excellent (नगोत्तम) 6. 7. 3; all the six mountains are frequented by the Siddhas and the Cāraṇas (सिद्धचारणसेविताः) 6. 7. 4. C. Characteristics: All the six mountains are full of jewels (षड् एते रत्नपर्वताः) 6. 7. 2; the serpents and the Nāgas live on the Niṣadha (सर्पा नागाश् च निषधे) 6. 7. 48; also the Gandharvas live there (गन्धर्वा निषधे शैले) 6. 7. 49. D. Past event: One of the mountains seen by Mārkaṇḍeya in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 = Nārāyaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 102. E. Impor-tance: Finds place in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 26, 2.

Niṣadha m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada and its people; the people also called Naiṣadba (3. 58. 18). A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (निषादा निषधाः) 6. 10. 50. B. Des-cription: Skilled in fighting while riding elephants (गजयुद्धेषु कुशलाः) 8. 17. 3; (गजयोधिन्) 8. 17. 2. C. Epic events: On the sixteenth day of war, the Niṣadha warriors, incited by Duryodhana, attacked Dhṛṣṭadyumna 8. 17. 3; they showered arrows, तोमरस् and नाराच type of arrows on Dhṛṣṭadyumna 8. 17. 4 (the war described in 8. 17. 5ff.). D. Past events: (1) Indra once took resort to a hermitage on a mountain in the Niṣadha country and lived there in disguise in order to subdue his enemies (इन्द्रेण निषधान् प्राप्य गिरिप्रस्थाश्रमे तदा । छन्नेनोष्य कृतं कर्म) 3. 299. 11; (2) The swan returned to the Niṣadha country and repor-ted to Nala his meeting with Damayanti (पुनर् आगम्य निषधान् नले सर्वं न्यवेदयत्) 3. 50. 31; Kali dwelt for a long time in the Niṣadha country looking for an opportunity to enter Nala's body (स नित्यम् अन्तरप्रेक्षी निषधेष्व् अवसच् चिरम्) 3. 56. 2; Kali told Puṣkara to play a game of dice with Nala, defeat him, and obtain the kingdom of the Niṣadha country (निषधान् प्रतिपद्यस्व) 3. 56. 5; the people of Niṣadha paid no regard to Nala after his defeat since they were threatened by Puṣkara (न सत्कारम् अकुर्वन् मयि नैषधाः) 3. 58. 18; Nala went to the Niṣadha country to challenge Puṣkara for a game of dice (जगाम निषधान् प्रति) 3. 77. 1. E. Nala (and his father Vīrasena) variously called the king of the Niṣadhas, the guardian of the lineage of Niṣadha, or one belong-ing to the Niṣadha country: (1) गोप्ता निषधवंशस्य: Nala 3. 61. 74; (2) निषधाधिप: Nala 3. 54. 19; 3. 59. 5, 18; 3. 61. 26; 3. 65. 3; 3. 75. 1; 3. 76. 11; 3. 77. 29; (3) निषधाधिपति: Nala 3. 58. 12; 3. 61. 32, 73; 3. 70. 29; निषधानां अधिपतिः: Nala 3. 61. 51, 88, 100; (4) निषधानां जनाधिप: 3. 61. 12; निषधानां जनाधिपः: Nala 3. 61. 82; (5) निषधेश्वर: Nala 3. 63. 19; (6) निषधेषु नृपोत्तमः: Vīrasena 3. 61. 45; (7) निषधेषु महीपतिः: Nala 3. 50. 3, 26; (8) निषधेषु महीपालः: वीरसेन 3. 49. 39; (9) नैषध: (i) Nala 1. 1. 175; 3. 50. 15, 20; 3. 51. 28, 29; 3. 52. 3, 8. 9; 3. 54. 17, 21, 24, 25, 28, 29, 30, 31; 3. 56. 1, 13, 14; 3. 57. 15; 3. 58. 7, 23; 3. 60. 2, 8, 15, 21, 23, 24; 3. 61. 54, 87, 119; 3. 63. 10; 3. 64. 1, 19; 3. 65. 5, 22, 23; 3. 66. 2; 3. 68. 2; 3. 70. 34, 35; 3. 71. 11, 14, 31, 33, 34; 3. 72. 14; 3. 73. 26; 3. 75. 4; 3. 76. 10, 11, 17; 3. 77. 1, 11, 12, 25; 3. 85. 20; 13. 75. 25 (भूरि-द्युम्नो नैषधः सोमकश् च । Does नैषध refer to Nala, or is it an adj. of Bhūridyumna ?) (ii) A certain warrior (king ?), not named, on the side of the Kauravas (नैषधश् च महाबलः) 7. 19. 13.
निष्कुट: Niṣkuṭa m.: Name of a mountain (?) A mountain range of the Himālayas (?); Arjuna, in his expedition to the north, conquered it along with the mountain Himavant; from there he went to the Śveta mountain (स विनिर्जित्य संग्रामे हिम-वन्तं सनिष्कुटम् । श्वेतपर्वतम् आसाद्य न्यवसत् पुरुषर्सभः ॥ ) 2. 24. 27 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 27. 29: निष्कुटं शैलविशेषम्).
नीलिका: Nīlikā f.: Name of a river. Mentioned in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 22, 2.
नेमिपर्वत: Nemiparvata m.: Name of a mountain. One who bathes on the Nemi mountain washes off his sin and goes to heaven 13. 26. 12.
नैमिष: Naimiṣa1 nt., Naimiṣakuñja, Naimiṣeyaḥ kuñjaḥ m.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Location: On the river Sarasvatī in the Kurukṣetra (ततो नैमिषकुञ्जं च समासाद्य … । ऋषयः … कुरुक्षेत्रं गताः पुरा ॥ ततः कुञ्जः सरस्वत्यां कृतो भरतसत्तम) 3. 81. 92-93; 9. 36. 48, 50, 54. B. Origin: The sages once went to the Kurukṣetra to perform long sessions of sacrifice but were disappointed as there was no room for them; hence Sarasvatī created many Kuñjas there and returned; these Kuñjas together came to be known as the Naimiṣeya Kuñja (एवं स कुञ्जो राजेन्द्र नैमिषेय इति स्मृतः) 9. 36. 48-51, 54; (ततः कुञ्जः सरस्वत्यां कृतो भरतसत्तम । ऋषीणाम् अवकाशः स्याद् यथा … ॥ ) 3. 81. 93. C. Description: Holy (पुण्य) 3. 82. 53; 13. 105. 45; 13. 151. 18; always holy (नित्यं पुण्यम्) 3. 82. 57; ritually pure (मेध्य) 3. 82. 57; resorted to by the Siddhas (सिद्धनिषेवित) 3. 82. 53. D. Holy: (1) Naimiṣa looked upon as holy on the whole earth (पृथिव्यां नैमिषं पुण्यम्) 3. 81. 173 (Nī., who takes नैमिष to mean the religious merit acquired in the Naimiṣa forest (see the next entry), on Bom. Ed. 3. 83. 202: नैमिषं नैमिषारण्ये कृतम् पुण्यम् पृथिव्याम् एव संततिसंपत्तिसार्वभौमादिपदप्रा-प्तिहेतुर् इत्य् अर्थः); (2) By taking a bath (अभिषेक) in this तीर्थ one who is controlled and lives on limited food secures the fruit of a Gavāmayana sacrifice and purifies his lineage up to the seventh generation 3. 82. 56; the bath (स्नात्वा) इन् the तीर्थ secures for the person the fruit of gifting a thousand cows 3. 81. 94; the bath (उपस्पृश्य कृतोदकः) secures for one who has controlled his sense organs the fruit of a Puruṣamedha 13. 26. 32; one who bathes (विगाह्य) in the ample waters of the Naimiṣa wakes up in the Vimāna praised by the Apsarases 9. 36. 35; (3) More than bathing in waters one should bathe in (i. e. practise) austerities at this तीर्थ (?) (अद्भ्यो भूयः प्लाव्यं तपसा वै शरीरं) 12. 286. 37 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 12. 297. 37: अद्भ्यः अद्भिः तपसा च शरीरं प्लाव्यं शोधनो ऽयं (? शोधनीयम्) तत्र आपः (? अपः) त्यक्त्वा); (4) The wise declare that one who abandons life at the Naimiṣa by fasting goes to heaven 3. 82. 57; (5) Those that are high-souled, have observed vows and who resort to this तीर्थ become auspicious and reach the Goloka (? गवां विमाने 13. 105. 44). 13. 105. 45 (for other details see Gayaśiras). E. Importance: (1) Brahman always lives there together with hosts of gods 3. 82. 53; (2) Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 18, 2. F. Past event: The sages living in the Naimiṣa forest once went to the Kuru-kṣetra on a pilgrimage (ऋषयः … नैमिषेयास् तपोधनाः । तीर्थयात्रां पुरस्कृत्य कुरु-क्षेत्रं गताः पुरा) 3. 81. 92-93. G. Limitation: Bhagīratha told Brahmadeva that he had not reached the Ṛṣiloka (13. 106. 5; Brahmaloka according to 13. 106. 39) by giving cows in large numbers as gifts at the Naimiṣa (but due to तपस् 13. 106. 41) 13. 106. 37.

Naimiṣa2, Naimiṣāraṇya nt.: Name of a forest. A. Location: In the east 3. 85. 3; 1. 207. 5-6; the river Gomatī flows along the Naimiṣa forest and the city Hāstinapura is situated near it (नैमिषे गोमतीतीरे यत्र नागाह्वयं पुरम्) 12. 343. 2; the river Utpalinī flows close to it 1. 207. 6. B. Holiness: (1) There are many very holy तीर्थस् sacred to gods in the Naimiṣa forest 3. 85. 4, and on the river Gomatī 3. 93. 1-2; (2) One who desires to go to the Naimiṣa forest destroys half of his sin; as soon as he enters it he is freed of all sins (नैमिषं प्रार्थयानस्य पापस्यार्धं प्रणश्यति । प्रविष्टमात्रस् तु नरः सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥ ) 3. 82. 54; (3) One who wants to visit तीर्थस् (तीर्थतत्परः) should live in the Naimiṣa for a month for all the तीर्थस् on the earth are present there (पृथिव्यां यानि तीर्थानी नैमिषे तानि भारत) 3. 82. 55. C. Epic events: (1) Kulapati Śaunaka was engaged in a twelve yearly sacrificial session in this forest at which Sūta Ugraśravas arrived 1. 1. 1; 1. 4. 1; the sages living in the Naimiṣa forest surrounded Ugaśravas to listen various narratives from him 1. 1. 3; Ugraśravas narrated the eighteen पर्वन्स् of the Mahābhārata to the sages in this forest 1. 2. 71; (2) Arjuna, during his exile, passed by the river Utpalinī flowing along the Naimiṣa forest after he descended from the slopes of the Himavant and then proceeded to the east 1. 207. 6; (3) from the Kāmyaka forest the Pāṇḍavas entered the Naimiṣa forest and bathed in the तीर्थस् of the Gomatī 3. 93. 1; (4) Bala-rāma went to the तीर्थ where the Sarasvatī returned for the sake of the sages living in the Naimiṣa forest (ऋषीणां नैमिषेयाणाम्) 9. 36. 35. D. Past events: (1) King Yayāti, while descending from the heaven, saw four kings Pratardana, Vasumanas, Śibi and Aṣṭaka, in the Naimiṣa forest performing a Vājapeya sacrifice and he chose to fall among them 5. 119. 9; (2) Baka Dālbhya after receiving a large number of cattle saved the kingdom of Dhṛtarāṣṭra from perishing and returned to the Naimiṣa forest (मोक्ष-यित्वा ततो राष्ट्रं प्रतिगृह्य पशून् बहून् । हृष्टात्मा नैमिषारण्यं जगाम पुनर् एव ह ॥ ) 9. 40. 24; (3) The ascetics living in the Naimiṣa forest (ऋषयः … नैमिषेयास् तपोधनाः) left for Kurukṣetra when they started for a तीर्थयात्रा 3. 81. 92; (4) Sages coming together (from different places) lived in the Naimiṣa forest; when once they performed a सत्र there they thought of the river Sarasvatī; when the river arrived it was known there as Kāñcanākṣī 9. 37. 15, 18; (5) Formerly, once, when a twelve-yearly सत्र of the ascetics living in the Naimiṣa (नैमिषेयाणाम्) was over and they had also performed the Viśvajit they left for the Pāñcālas to ask Dakṣiṇā from the king Kṛṣṇa 9. 40. 3; (6) The old men living in the Naimiṣa forest (नैमिषारण्य-वासिनः) used to characterize the narrative of Āstīka, composed by Dvaipāyana, as an old Itihāsa (इतिहासम् इमं वृद्धाः पुरा-णं परिचक्षते) 1. 13. 6; (7) Formerly, once, when gods offered a सत्र, Vaivasvata (Yama) acted as a Śamitṛ (तत्र वैवस्वतो राजञ् शामित्रम् अकरोत् तदा) 1. 189. 1 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 197. 1: शमिता यज्ञे पशुवधकर्ता तस्य कर्म शामित्रम्); (8) Formerly, in the Kṛtayuga, the ascetics in the Naimiṣa forest (नैमिषेयास् तपस्-विनः) were engaged in a twelve-yearly sacrificial session for which many sages arrived 9. 36. 39-40; (9) The wheel of Dharma, in tune with the one in the former creation, was set in motion in the Naimiṣa forest (यत्र पूर्वाभिसर्गेण धर्म-चक्रं प्रवर्तितम् । नैमिषे) 12. 343. 2. E. Importance: People of the region of the Naimiṣa (सनैमिषाः, आ नैमिषात्, नैमिषाः) know the Dharma, follow the Dharma (धर्-मं जानन्ति शाश्वतम्; धर्मं पुराणम् उपजीवन्ति सन्तः; जानन्ति धर्मम्) 8. 30. 60-62, 75.

Naimiṣa, Naimiṣeya m. (pl.): The people and the sages living in the Naimiṣa forest. A. The people: They are mentioned among those people who knew the eternal धर्म (मत्स्याः सनैमिषाः … धर्मं जानन्ति शाश्वतम्) 8. 30. 60-61; (कुरवो नैमिषाश् च … जानन्ति धर्मम्) 8. 30. 75. B. The sages: (1) The Naimiṣeya sages once started on a pilgrimage and first went to Kurukṣetra (नैमिषेयास् तपोधनाः । तीर्थयात्रां पुरस्कृत्य कुरुक्षेत्रं गताः पुरा ॥ ) 3. 81. 92; (2) The Naimiṣeya sages of the Kṛtayuga once performed a सत्र lasting for twelve years (पूर्वं कृतयुगे राजन् नैमिषेयास् तपस्विनः ।  … सत्रे द्वादशवार्षिके) 9. 36. 39, 35. [For Naimiṣa forest, see Vol. I. pp. 377-379].
नौबन्धन: Naubandhana nt.: Name of the highest peak (शृङ्ग) of the Himavant. The highest peak of the mountain Himavant to which the ark of Manu was tied by the seven sages was known as Naubandhana even in the days of the narrator of the Mahābhārata (तच् च नौबन्धनं नाम शृङ्गं हिमवतः परम् । ख्यातम् अद्यापि कौन्तेय) 3. 185. 45-47.
नन्दाश्रम: Nandāśrama m.: Name of an आश्रम। One of the holy places and आश्रमस् (पुण्येषु देशेषु 5. 187. 24) where the prin-cess of Kāśi (Ambā) stayed to practise austerities for the death of Bhīṣma 5. 187. 25; all the आश्रमस् were of high-souled as-cetics who were extremely pious (आश्रमं पुण्यशीलानां तापसानां महात्मनाम्) 5. 187. 23; at these holy places the princess bathed day and night and practised auste-rities (तत्र पुण्येषु देशेषु साप्लुताङ्गी दिवानिशम् । व्यचरत् काशिकन्या सा) 5. 187. 24; (एतेषु तीर्थेषु … आप्लावयत गात्राणि तीव्रम् आस्थाय वै तपः) 5. 187. 28.
नन्दिग्राम: Nandigrāma m.: Name of a village. During Rāma's term of exile, Bharata, stayed at Nandigrāma and ruled from there keeping before him Rāma's sandals (नन्दि-ग्रामे ऽकरोद् राज्यं पुरस्कृत्यास्य पादु-के) 3. 261. 38; when Rāma returned to Ayodhyā, he first sent Hanūmant as his messenger to Bharata; Hanūmant met Bharata at Nandigrāma and told him the good news (of Rāma's return); when Hanūmant returned after meeting Bharata, Rāma went to Nandigrāma 3. 275. 60.
नरनारायणाश्रम: Naranārāyaṇāśrama, Nārāyaṇāśrama1 m.: Name of a very holy hermitage, also called Naranārāyaṇasthāna (1. 64. 24; 3. 145. 37), Nārāyaṇasthāna (3. 174. 9). A. Location: Listed by Lomaśa among the holy places in the north (उदीच्यां … दिशि) 3. 88. 1; situated on the Gandha-mādana mountain (पर्वतं गन्धमाद-नम् । … यत्र नरनाराय्व्णाश्रमः) 3. 142. 22-23; on a place near the large Badarī tree (नारायणः … । तस्य … पुण्यां विशालां बदरीम् अनु । आश्रमः ख्यायते) 3. 88. 21-22; 3. 142. 23; 3. 145. 17, 23; 3. 174. 8-9; 12. 126. 2-3; the river Bhāgīrathī flew near it (नरनारायणस्थानं भागीरथ्योप-शोभितम्) 3. 145. 37; (नरनारायण-स्थानं गङ्गयेवोपशोभितम्) 1. 64. 24; near the Kailāsa mountain (कईलासम् … । तस्याभ्याशे तु ददृशुर् नरनारायणा-श्रमम्) 3. 145. 15-16. B. Descrip-tion: Resorted to by the sages Nara and Nārāyaṇa (नरनारायणाश्रित) 3. 145. 23; (आश्रमम् … । रेमाते यत्र तौ नित्यं नरनारायणाव् ऋषी) 12. 126. 4-5; holy (पुण्य) 3. 88. 22; 3. 145. 23, 24, 35; heavenly (दिव्य) 3. 145. 26, 28; 12. 126. 2; pleasing (मनोरम) 3. 145. 35; indescriba-ble (अनिर्देश्य) 3. 145. 28; full of splend-our (शोभया युक्तम्) 3. 145. 36; endowed with lustre (श्रिया युतम्) 3. 145. 28; shin-ing with brahmanical lustre (ब्राह्म्या लक्ष्म्या समन्वितम्) 3. 145. 25; looking like the residence of Śakra (शक्रसदन-प्रख्य) 3. 145. 35; comparable to heaven (स्वर्गोपम) 3. 145. 35; famous in the three worlds (त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः) 3. 88. 22; fit to be resorted to (आश्रयणीय) 3. 145. 28; removing fatigue (श्रमनाशन) 3. 145. 28; destroying sorrow (शोकनाशन) 3. 145. 24; free from the afflictions caused by hunger, thirst, cold and heat (क्षुत्तृट्-शीतोष्णदोषैश् च वर्जितम्) 3. 145. 24; free from wrath and greed (अपेतक्रोधलोभो ऽयं आश्रमः) 5. 94. 21; free from dark-ness (तमसा रहितम्) 3. 145. 24; not penetrated by the rays of the sun (अनादृ-ष्टं रवेह् करैः) 3. 145. 24; honoured by gods and divine sages (देवदेवर्षिपूजित) 3. 145. 37; full of hosts of great sages (महर्षिगणसंबाध) 3. 145. 25; resor-ted to by great sages and ascetics (महर्-षिभिः … यतिभिः … उपेतम्) 3. 145. 29-30; offering shelter to all beings (शरण्यं सर्वभूतानां) 3. 145. 27; beautified by the service to gods (देवचर्योपशोभित) 3. 145. 28 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 145. 32: देव-चर्या सत्यसंकल्पत्वादिका); resounding with the sound of Vedic recitations (ब्रह्-मघोषनिनादित) 3. 145. 27; honoured by the बलि and fire offerings (बलिहोमार्चित) 3. 145. 26; having many large fire-halls (विशालैर् अग्निशरणैः … आचितम्) 3. 145. 27; full of heavenly trees always laden with flowers and fruits (उपेतं पादपैर् दिव्यैः सदापुष्पफलोपगैः) 3. 145. 16; well swept and well smeared (सुसंमृष्टानु-लेपन) 3. 145. 26 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 145. 29: सुष्ठु संमृष्टं संमार्जनम् अनु-लेपनं च यत्र); shining on all sides with the offerings of heavenly flowers (दिव्य-पुष्पोपहारैश् च सर्वतो ऽभिविराजितम्) 3. 145. 26; adorned with big and sturdy water vessels (महद्भिस् तोयकलशैः कठिनैश् चोपशोभितम्) 3. 145. 27 (but Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 145. 30: कठिनैः शिक्यैः करण्डैर् वा); filled with shining ladles and vessels (स्रुग्भाण्डैर् आचितं शुभैः) 3. 145. 27; difficult of access to men who were placed outside the pale of religion (दुष्प्रवेशं … नरैर् धर्मबहिष्कृतैः) 3. 145. 25. C. Characteristic: Aśvaśiras (Nārāyaṇa) recites the eternal Vedas in this आश्रम (यत्राश्वशिरा राजन् वेदान् पठति शाश्वतान्) 12. 126. 3. D. Epic events: (1) The Pāṇḍavas saw the आश्रम at Badarī: they enjoyed themselves there looking at different sights; they lived there for six nights anxious to meet Arjuna 3. 145. 23, 37, 39-43; 3. 146. 1; (2) After killing Jaṭāsura, the Pāṇḍavas returned to Nārāyaṇāśrama 3. 155. 1; (3) After meet-ing Arjuna, the Pāṇḍavas on their return journey, again stayed at the Nārāyaṇa-sthāna (ऊषुस् ततस् तत्र … नारायणस्थान-गता नराग्र्याः) 3. 174. 9. E. Past events: (1) Ṛṣabha, a brahmanical sage (विप्रर्षि), told king Sumitra that once, while he was on a pilgrimage, he happened to reach Naranārāyaṇāśrama; he bathed in the lake Vaihāyasa which was nearby, satisfied manes and gods according to the rites, and returned to the आश्रम; he stayed at a place not far from the आश्रम 12. 126. 2. 4-5; while living there he met a sage called Tanu and, later, king Vīradyumna who was searching his lost son Bhūridyumna; the sages in the आश्रम asked the king the purpose of his visiting the आश्रम 12. 126. 6, 14, 26-27; (2) Nara and Nārāyaṇa told king Dambhodbhava who sought a duel with them that the आश्रम was not the right place for a duel, nor for the use of weapons, nor for the practice of false-hood (न ह्य् अस्मिन्न् आश्रमे युद्धं कुतः शस्त्रं कुतो ऽनृजुः) 5. 94. 21. F. Simile: The आश्रम of Kaṇva along the river Mālinī looked like the Naranārāyaṇasthāna along the river Gaṅgā (अलंकृतं … मालि-न्या … नरनारायणस्थानं गङ्गयेवोप-शोभितम्) 1. 64. 24. [See Badarī, Badaryā-śrama]
नागाह्वय: Nāgāhvaya2 nt.: Name of the city of the Nāga Padmanābha (Padma). A. Location: Situated in the Naimiṣa forest on the bank of the river Gomatī (नै-मिषे गोमतीतीरे तत्र नागाह्वयं पुरम्) 12. 343. 2; 12. 345. 12; 12. 349. 4; Nāga Padmanābha, also called Padma, resided there 12. 343. 4; hence called the resort of the lord of the नागास् (भुजगेन्द्र-संश्रय) 12. 344. 10. B. Past events: (1) All the gods once performed a sacri-fice at Nāgāhvaya (समग्रैस् त्रिदशैस् तत्र इष्टम् आसीत्) 12. 343. 3; (2) Here king Māndhātṛ offended Indra (यत्रेन्द्राति-क्रमं चक्रे मान्धाता) 12. 343. 3; (3) Atithi proceeded to Nāgāhvaya to meet Padmanābha 12. 344. 10.
नारायणाश्रम: Nārāyaṇāśrama2 m.: Name of a her-mitage. Located near the lakes of Rāma near Kurukṣetra (कुरुक्षेत्रस्य मध्यतः) 3. 126. 42; shown by Lomaśa to Yudhiṣṭhira (पश्य रामह्रदान् एतान् पश्य नारायणा-श्रमम्) 3. 129. 6.
निर्मोचन: Nirmocana nt.: Name of a city. Six thousand great Asuras tried to bind Kṛṣṇa with snares at Nirmocana, but they did not succeed; Kṛṣṇa cut off those sharp snares, killed the six thousand Asuras and Mura, and then proceeded to Nirmo-cana (निर्मोचने षट्सहस्राः पाशैर् बद्ध्वा महासुराः । ग्रहीतुं नाशकंश् चैनम्) 5. 128. 43 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 5. 130. 45: निर्मोचने नगरविशेषे); (निर्मो-चने षट्सहस्राणि हत्वा संछिद्य पाशान् सहसा क्षुरान्तान् । मुरं हत्वा … निर्मो-चनं चापि जगाम वीरः) 5. 47. 77 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 5. 48. 83: निर्मोचने नगरे).
नग्नजित्: Nagnajit m. (pl.): Name of a people. Described as very difficult to be con-quered (सुदुर्जय) 8. 57. 31; Śalya reminded Karṇa that he had once defeated with great firmness Nagnajit people in battle (नग्नजितस् त्वया) । … यया धृत्या जिताः संख्ये सुदुर्जयाः) 8. 57. 31.
नन्दिवेग: Nandivega m. (pl.): Name of a people. Bhīma mentioned Śama as the king of the Nandivegas; he was one of the eighteen famous kings who were born at the end of the युग and who extirpated their kinsmen, friends and relatives (अष्टादशेमे राजानः प्रख्याता … । … शंअश् च नन्दि-वेगानाम् … युगान्ते कृष्ण संभूताः) 5. 72. 11, 17.
नलकालक: Nalakālaka m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा … ) 6. 10. 56, 5; (सोद्भिदा नलकालकाः) 6. 10. 58.
नवराष्ट्र: Navarāṣṭra nt. (sg.): Name of a country (राष्ट्र) also called Janapada. A. Location: Around the Kurus (वासाय राष्ट्राणि कीर्तयिष्यामि … ॥ … जनपदा … परितः कुरून्) 4. 1. 8-9. B. Description: pleasing (रमणीय) 4. 1. 8; (रम्य) 4. 1. 9; having ample food (बह्वन्न) 4. 1. 9; well-protected (गुप्त) 4. 1. 8. C. Epic event: (1) Sahadeva in his expedition to the south before the Rājasūya (सहदेवस् तु दक्षिणां 2. 23. 9; प्रययौ दक्षिणां दिशम् 2. 28. 1, 8, 37) conquered Navarāṣṭra before marching on the Kuntibhoja 2. 28. 6; (2) Listed by Arjuna among those countries in one of which the Pāṇḍavas could live during their period of अज्ञातवास (दशार्णा नव-राष्ट्रं च) 4. 1. 9.
नाकुल: Nākula m. (pl.): Name of a people (?). On the second day of war, Nākulas and others, led by Nakula and Sahadeva, stood on the left side of the Krauñcāruṇa-vyūha (6. 46. 39; Krauñca 6. 47. 1) of the Pāṇḍavas (सह नाकुलैः … वामं पार्-श्वं समाश्रिताः) 6. 46. 51; (name of a people, or characterization of the warriors led by Nakula ?)
नागद्वीप: Nāgadvīpa nt. (sg.): Name of a द्वीप। The shape of the Sudarśanadvīpa (= Jambudvīpa) when reflected in the moon looked like a hare; Nāgadvīpa for-med one of the two ‘ears’ of the hare, the other ear being Kaśyapadvīpa (यथा च पुरुषः पश्येद् आदर्शे मुखम् आत्मनः । एवं सुदर्शनद्वीपो दृश्यते चन्द्र-मण्डले ॥ ) 6. 6. 15; (कर्णौ तु नागद्वी-पं च कश्यपद्वीपम् एव च ॥ ) 6. 7. 52.
नारायण: Nārāyaṇa m. (pl.): Name of a class of Gopas or Gopālas; their army referred to as Nārāyaṇabala. A. Description: All Nārāyṇas acted as warriors (सर्वे संग्रामयोधिनः) 5. 7. 16; as warriors, equal to Kṛṣṇa in firmness (मत्संहननतुल्य) 5. 7. 16; difficult to be assailed in war (ते वा युधि दुराधर्षा  … ) 5. 7. 17; fierce in war (युद्धदुर्मद) 9. 2. 36; in wars, they fought with weapons of different kinds (विविधायुधपाणि) 7. 18. 7. B. Epic events: (1) A large number of Gopas called Nārayaṇas, an अर्बुद strong, were taken by Duryodhana to fight from his side (गोपानाम् अर्बुदं महत् । नारायाणा इति ख्याताः) 5. 7. 16; (सहस्राणां सहस्रं तु) 5. 7. 20-21; (2) On the twelfth day of war, the fleeing Nārāyaṇa Gopālas who formed a part of the army of the Saṃśaptakas, incited by Suśarman, returned to the battlefield deter-mined to fight till death (संशप्तकगणाः पुनः । नारायणाश् च गोपालाः कृत्वा मृत्युं निवर्तनम्) 7. 17. 31; the angry Nārāyaṇas surrounded Arjuna and covered him with arrows; they made both Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna invisible for a while; Arjuna employed त्वाष्ट्र अस्त्र against them; bewildered by the अस्त्र, they killed each other; the अस्त्र reduced to ashes the arrows released by Nārāyaṇas and killed them 7. 18. 7-8, 11-15; later in the day, Arjuna fought with the remainder of the Saṃśaptakas and Nārāyaṇas stationed to the right side of the army (दक्षिणेन तु सेनायाः कुरुते कदनं बली । सं-शप्तकावशेषस्य नारायणबलस्य च) 7. 30. 29; (3) On the fourteenth day, the Nārāyaṇa Gopālas tried to check the march of Arjuna in the direction of Jaya-dratha; they were determined to risk their lives while fighting with Arjuna (नारायणाश् च गोपालाः … त्यक्त्वात्मानो ऽर्जुनं प्रति) 7. 66. 38-39; (4) On the sixteenth day, the army of the Nārayaṇa Gopālas stood at the left foot of the Makaravyūha (8. 7. 14) of the Kauravas: they were led by Kṛtavarman (कृतवर्मा व्यवस्थितः । नारायणबलैर् युक्तो गोपालैर् … ) 8. 7. 17; they (नारायणबलं च यत्) and the Saṃśaptakas attacked Arjuna 8. 19. 2; (5) On the seventeenth day, Arjuna killed the army of the Nārāyaṇas (नारायणबलं च यत्) and the Kosalas and the Saṃ-śaptakas 8. 37. 2; (6) Mentioned by Dhṛtarāṣṭra among those who were killed in the war (नारायणा हता यत्र गोपाला … ) 9. 2. 36.
निषाद: Niṣāda m. (pl.): Name of a people of low caste; their territory called निषाद-विषय 7. 168. 35; 14. 84. 7; निषादराष्ट्र 3. 130. 4; निषादभूमि 2. 28. 5; their settle-ment निषादालय 1. 24. 2; 12. 315. 14 (निषादानाम् आलयः). A. Origin: (1) Sages killed Ati-bala's son Vena with Kuśa blades and produced from his right thigh a dwarfish person (ह्रस्वाङ्गः); they asked him to sit down; from him Niṣādas were born (निषीद इत्य् एवम् ऊचुस् तम् ऋषयो ब्रह्मवादिनः । तस्मान् निषादाः संभूताः) 12. 59. 102-103; (this is also an etymological explana-tion); (2) Niṣādas were born due to intermixture of the original four castes (निषादाः … । एते चतुर्भ्यो वर्णेभ्यो जायन्ते वै परस्परम्) 12. 285. 8-9. B. Location: (1) Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; शका निषादा … ) 6. 10. 50; in the west: the Vina-śana tīrtha on the river Sarasvatī called the gate of the Niṣādarāṣṭra 3. 130. 4; the territory of Niṣādas was located outside the Samantapañcaka 7. 168. 35; 7. 121. 24, 34; (2) Another territory in the south-west: Sahadeva in his expedition to the south of Indraprastha (प्रययौ दक्षिणां दिशम् 2. 28. 1; 2. 23. 9) conquered the land of the Niṣādas (निषादभूमिम् … व्यजयत्) 2. 28. 5; south of Śūrpāraka 2. 28. 43-44; Arjuna went from the Daśārṇa country to the country of Niṣādas 14. 84. 5-7; from the country of Niṣādas, he went to the southern ocean (प्रययौ भूयः दक्षिणं सलिलार्णवम्) 14. 84. 10; (3) In a past event, a settlement of the Niṣādas is said to be in a solitary place in the bay of the ocean (समुद्र-कुक्षाव् एकान्ते निषादालयम् उत्तमम्) 1. 24. 2. C. Low Status: A son be-gotten on a Kṣatriya woman by a Śūdra becomes Niṣāda 13. 48. 12; a Niṣāda unit-ing with a Vaidehī begets Āhiṇḍika 13. 48. 27; a Niṣāda uniting with a woman of lower caste begets a Mudgara and Dāśa who lives by plying boats (दाशं नावोपजीवि-नम्) 13. 48. 21; a Niṣāda also begets a Madranābha who rides in vehicles drawn by asses (निषादान् मद्रनाभं च खर-यानप्रयायिनम्) 13. 48. 23; (2) A Niṣādī from a Caṇḍāla gives birth to a son who lives on the outskirts on the crema-tion grounds; he is an outcaste among out-castes (निषादी चापि चण्डालात् पुत्रम् अन्ता-वसायिनम् । श्मशानगोचरं सूते बाह्यैर् अपि बहिष्कृतम् ॥ ) 13. 48. 28. D. Profe-ssion: They lived by catching fish (मत्स्य-जीविनः; जालहस्ताः; मत्स्योद्धरणनिश्चि-ताः; निश्चिता जालकर्मणि) 13. 50. 11, 12; (निषादो मत्स्यघ्नः) 13. 48. 12; hence also called कैवर्ताः 13. 50. 14. E. Des-cription: (i) Their settlement in the ocean is said to be excellent (उत्तम) 1. 24. 2; (ii) People and warriors: residing on mountains and in forests (शैलवना-श्रय) 12. 59. 103; strong and brave, they never returned from water-reservoirs (empty-handed out of fear) (व्यायता बलिनः शूराः सलिलेष्व् अनिवर्तिनः) 13. 50. 12; cruel (क्रूर) 12. 59. 103; skilled in fighting with elephants (गजयोधिनः, गजयुद्धेषु कुशलाः) 8. 17. 2-3; their elephants often mentioned during war-descriptions cf. 6. 50. 7; 7. 45. 21-22; 8. 12. 59; 8. 15. 8; 8. 17. 5, 22; 8. 33. 1, 4; 8. 43. 70; 8. 49. 78-79. F. Their abode used for comparison: The mountain Himālaya without the sound of Vedic recitation appeared like an abode of the Niṣādas (न भ्राजते यथापूर्वं निषादा-नाम् इवालयः । … वेदध्वनिनिराकृतः) 12 315. 14. G. Epic events: (1) Sahadeva, in his expedition to the south before the Rājasūya, conquered the territory of the Niṣādas and brought them under control (निषादभूमिम् … व्यजयत्) 2. 28. 5; (वशे चक्रे … निषादान्) 2. 28. 44; (2) Karṇa had once defeated them and made them pay tribute (चक्रे बलिभृतः पुरा) 8. 5. 19-20 (possibly a reference to Karṇa's conquest of the earth before the Vaiṣṇava sacrifice performed by Duryodhana 3. 241, 32 and Cr. Edn. Vol. 3, App. I. 24. 28-72); (3) On the second day of the war, Yudhi-ṣṭhira with Niṣādas (on the side of the Pāṇḍavas) and other warriors, formed the ‘back’ of the Krauñcāruṇavyūha 6. 46. 39. 47 (Krauñca 6. 47. 1); (4) On the same day, Ketumant, a Niṣāda prince (नैषादि) with his Niṣāda warriors (on the side of the Kauravas), riding elephants, surrounded Bhīma (अयुतेन गजानां च निषादैः सह केतुमान्); Cedis and other warriors led by Bhīma, attacked Niṣādas; in the fierce battle, Niṣādas and Kaliṅgas outnumbered Cedis and their associates (विमर्दः सुमहान् आसीद् अल्पानां बहुभिः सह) 6. 50. 5, 7, 8, 14; (5) On the tenth day, Niṣādas and other warriors, incited by Duryodhana, attacked Arjuna 6. 112. 108; (6) On the thirteenth day, Niṣādas and Kaliṅgas, riding elephants (गजानीकेन दंशिताः; कुञ्जरानीकम्) obstructed the advance of Abhimanyu; he scattered away their army of elephants 7. 45. 21-22; (7) On the fifteenth day, Dhṛṣṭadyumna regretted that he did not throw away the head of Droṇa in the territory of the Niṣādas, as (Arjuna did) the head of Jayadratha (यन् न तस्य शिरो मया । निषादविषये क्षिप्तं जयद्रथशिरो यथा) 7. 168. 35; (8) On the sixteenth day, Kaliṅga, Vaṅga and Niṣāda warriors, riding elephants (अथ द्विपैर् देवपति-द्विपाभैर्) rushed against Arjuna; Arjuna killed both the elephants and the warriors 8. 12. 59-60; (9) On the same day, the Pāṇḍya king killed many Niṣāda warriors, who fought with शक्ति, प्रास and quivers (i. e. arrows), along with their elephants (द्विरदान्) and horses 8. 15. 5, 8-9; (10) On the same day, incited by Duryodhana, Niṣādas, riding elephants (हस्तिभिस्), attack-ed Dhṛṣṭadyumna with arrows, तोमरस् and नाराच arrows; Dhṛṣṭadyumna showered नाराच arrows on them to crush their elephants 8. 17. 1, 3-5; (11) On the same day, they attacked Nakula with arrows and तोमरस्; when warriors came to help Nakula, a fierce battle took place between chariot-riders and elephant-riders (युद्धं रथिनां हस्तिभिः सह) 8. 17. 20-22; (12) On the seventeenth day, Karṇa killed many warriors in the army of Yudhi-ṣṭhira consisting of Niṣādas (on the side of the Pāṇḍavas) and others; when they began to run away, Sātyaki incited them to fight; on return, they were killed by Karṇa who cut off their arms and removed their head-gears (ते विबाहुशिरस्त्राणाः … पेतुः पृथिव्यां … ) 8. 33. 1, 4-5; (13) On the same day, Arjuna referred to Bhīma's killing Niṣādas (on the side of the Kauravas) and their elephants (नाग-वरान् … सदामदान् नीलबलाहकोपमान्) 8. 49. 78-79; (14) When Arjuna moved with the Aśvamedha horse, he had to fight a fierce battle with the Niṣādas led by Ekalavya's son 14. 84. 7-8. H. Mythologi-cal event: Vinatā allowed her son Garuḍa to eat Niṣādas (but not the Brāhmaṇas) while on his way to fetch अमृत 1. 24. 2; when Garuḍa found the Niṣādas he colle-cted them together; then, opening his beak wide, he stood in the way of the Niṣādas; they entered Garuḍa's mouth by hundreds since they were deluded by the dust raised by the wind; the hungry Garuḍa closed his beak and killed many Niṣādas 1. 24. 10-14. I. Past events: (1) Sarasvatī disappeared at the gate of the Niṣādarāṣṭra so that the Niṣādas might not see her 3. 130. 4; (2) Some Niṣādas once came to the place where Cyavana was practising austerities near the confluence of Gaṅgā and Yamunā; the Niṣādas who wanted to catch fishes threw their net in water; when they drew their net they dragged Cyavana along with fishes; they fell at the feet of Cyavana and asked him what they should do; Cyavana told the Niṣadas that he did not want to forsake the fishes and hence would get killed or sold along with them; afraid, the Niṣādas reported the matter to king Nahuṣa; Nahuṣa asked his priest to pay one thousand (coins) to the Niṣādas as the price of fishes and Cyavana; on Cyavana's denial to accept this price, Nahuṣa went on bidding higher and higher price to be paid to Niṣādas; ultimately Cyavana was purchased by giving a cow to Niṣādas; they offered it to Cyavana; Cyavana sent the Niṣādas and the fishes to heaven 13. 50. 3-26; 13. 51. 1-41. I. Some persons called the king of Niṣādas or one belong-ing to the Niṣādas: (1) निषादराज: (i) Ekalavya 5. 47. 71; (ii) Hiraṇyadhanus 1. 123. 10; (2) निषादराजन्: Ekalavya 14. 84. 7; (3) निषादाधिपति: (i) Hiraṇya-dhanus 1. 123. 24, 28; 2. 27. 10 (?) (ii) a certain Mahāsura 1. 61. 48; (4) नैषादि: (i) Ekalavya: 1. 123. 11, 17, 18, 29, 38; 7. 156. 2, 17, 18; 16. 7. 10; (ii) Ekalavya's son 14. 84. 10; (iii) Ketumant 6. 50. 5; (iv) A Kuru warrior (not named; Eka-lavya ?) 8. 43. 70; (v) Kāpavya 12. 133. 3; (5) निषादज: Ekalavya 1. 123. 32; (6) निषाद: Ekalavya 7. 155. 29; (7) Niṣādī (f.), not named 12. 133. 3.
नीप: Nīpa m. (pl.): Name of a people. Past events: (1) Aṅgirases had once defeated them (नीपान् अङ्गिरसो ऽजयन्) 13. 34. 16; (2) Janamejaya, the king of the Nīpas, was mentioned by Bhīma among those eighteen kings who extirpated their kinsmen, friends and relatives (ये समुच्चिच्छिदुर् ज्ञातीन् सुहृदश् च सबान्ध-वान् … नीपानां जनमेजयः) 5. 72. 11, 13; (3) Their former kings were royal sages (राजर्षयः) 2. 8. 25, 7; they were pious, famous and learned and a hundred of them waited on Yama in his Sabhā (शतं नीपाः … एते राजर्षयः पुण्याः कीर्तिमन्तो बहुश्रुताः । तस्यां सभायां राजर्षे वैवस्वतम् उपासते ॥ ) 2. 8. 21, 25.
नीलायुध: Nīlāyudha m. (pl.): Name of a people (?) A. Location: They lived in the south (दक्षिणापथवासिभिः) 5. 19. 23. B. Description: Possessed of great heroic qualities (महावीर्य) 5. 19. 23. C. Epic events: (1) King Nīla of Māhiṣmatī, along with the Nīlāyudha warriors, one अक्षौहिणी strong, joined the army of Duryodhana (नीलो नीलायुधैः सह) 5. 19. 23; (2) On the third day of war, king Nīla, along with his Nīlāyudha warriors, (those on the side of the Pāṇḍa-vās ?) stood behind Virāṭa and Drupada at the southern tip (दक्षिणं शृङ्गम्) of the Ardhacandravyūha of the Pāṇḍavas 6. 52. 10-12. (But Nīla is said to have joined the Kaurava army, cf. Epic event No. 1).
नैरृत: Nairṛta m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada and its people. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (तथैवानर्तनैरृताः) 6. 10. 50. B. Epic event: In the arrangement of the army of the Kauravas before the start of the war, Bhṛhadbala, along with Nairṛtas who had taken up arms (नैरृतैर् आत्तशस्-त्रैः), guarded the army in the south (बलं त्वदीयं दक्षिणतो ऽभिपाति) 6. 20. 14.
